current.text: Brooklyn acquired him from Minnesota in the Nic Claxton trade.
He is a projected starter for Brooklyn, next to Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe.
He is the Nets' most accomplished on-ball creator and is expected to handle the ball a lot.
He has several years left on his contract and is staying in Brooklyn.
His usage should rise from about 27 to about 30, and his assists should go up. Sharing the ball with Michael Porter Jr. is seen as a better spot than playing second fiddle to Anthony Edwards.
His minutes are expected to drop to about 32 a night, from 34 to 35 last season. Blowouts and minutes for Noah Clowney may lower his upside.
Brooklyn does not control its own pick (it goes to Houston), so it has no reason to tank. It is still projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins.
Brooklyn has little to play for, so he may sit some games in March to give young players time. That overlaps with our fantasy playoffs.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. Its schedule in weeks 19 to 21 is 3-4-3, which is 10 games with one back-to-back.
Michael Porter Jr. is a trade candidate, and Brooklyn may move more minutes to Josh Minott, Noah Clowney and its young guards in the second half of the season.
Experts place him around pick 65 to 75 in category leagues. Mock drafts took him at 67 and 72. One expert sees upside to return to the top 50.
His ESPN rank near 86 is great value, and a Yahoo ADP near 68 is fine. In category leagues, take him a bit later than in points leagues.
In an auction mock, the expert hoped to pay about 10 USD, but he went for 15 USD.
His block conversion last season was 4.9%, well below his 9% career rate.
His blocks might recover a little in Brooklyn without Rudy Gobert next to him.

durable.text: His value comes from points, rebounds and assists. His assists are high for a forward.
He turns the ball over a lot, and that is his clearest weak category.
He gives little on defense in fantasy. His steals are average at best and his blocks are poor.
He shoots about 48% from the field and 80% from the line, so his percentages are close to neutral. His reputation for hurting percentages is not accurate.
He shot 32% from three in Minnesota and was treated as a non-shooter.
He is a classic player who is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues, though category leagues underrate him.

note: Randle is a mid-round forward who helps in points, rebounds and assists but costs you in turnovers and blocks. That makes him a natural fit for a punt TO build. The experts put him around picks 65 to 75, close to his Yahoo rank of 74 and ESPN rank of 84. In auctions he should cost about 10 to 15 USD (he went for 10 USD in our league last season and 15 USD in a mock). Early in the season, check that his minutes hold near 32 and his usage rises toward 30. Remember that Brooklyn may rest him in March, right in our playoff weeks, when the team has only 10 games.
